title: Finding Things by Position
description: How to get a specific item out of a list using its index.

blocks.content: You're building a leaderboard for a game. You have the top 5 scores stored in order, and you need to show the player in 3rd place. How do you get just that one score out of the list?

Every item in a list has a position, called an **index**. Python starts counting positions at 0, not 1. So the first item is at index 0, the second at index 1, and so on.

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["index 0: 512"] --- B["index 1: 488"] --- C["index 2: 470"] --- D["index 3: 455"]
```

blocks.question:
scores = [512, 488, 470, 455]

Which index gets the 3rd place score (470)?
blocks.explanation: 3rd place is the 3rd item, but indexing starts at 0, so it's at index 2, not 3.

blocks.prompt: You have a list of runners in finish order. Write a function `get_winner(runners)` that returns the name of whoever finished first.

tests.description: returns the first name in the list
works when there's only one runner
